prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description nitro registers every route rule under the base URL, but the probe paths we try do not have a base, so we were missing out on a perf optimisation when running nuxt with a base URL that was configured at build time 🤷

prs.title: fix(nuxt): handle rejected `updateCallbackDone` of aborted view transition
prs.author: 0xgdr
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

resolves #36626

### 📚 Description

With `experimental.viewTransition` enabled, a client-side navigation that fails (`router.onError`, `app:error` or `vue:error`, e.g. a page whose setup throws `createError`) logs `Uncaught (in promise) undefined`.

**Cause:** the plugin aborts the transition with `abortTransition()`, which rejects the promise returned from the update callback. Per the View Transitions spec that rejects `updateCallbackDone` as well as `ready` and `finished`. `finished` (#34515) and `ready` (#35537) are already caught, but `updateCallbackDone` isn't.

**Fix:** catch `updateCallbackDone` alongside the existing handlers.

**Tests:**

- In `test/nuxt/view-transitions.test.ts`, the mock's `updateCallbackDone` now follows the promise returned by the update callback, as in the browser.
- A new test fires `app:error` while the transition is in progress and asserts no unhandled rejection is reported. It fails on `main` and passes with the fix; the file's other 18 tests still pass. I haven't run the full suite locally.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: fix(nuxt): encode page paths before matching route rule keys
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description with route rules like this, `/café/about` never gets stubbed out of the client bundle, even though `/café/**` should cover it: ```ts routeRules: { '/café/**': { ssr: false }, '/café/secret': { ssr: true }, } ``` this is because of a divergence between h3 + `markPagesCoveredByRouteRule` (similarly to https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36682, this means we miss a perf optimisation) so this PR encodes each page pattern with the same character set h3 uses before checking coverage.

prs.title: fix(nuxt): match method-scoped route rules
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description h3 (now?) accepts method-scoped route rule keys, and nitro applies them per request method at runtime: ```ts routeRules: { 'GET /admin/**': { appMiddleware: 'auth' }, } ``` but this is not something we have hitherto handled in nuxt - we'd just end up handling that like an absolute path this PR parses the method prefix the same way h3's `parseRouteKey` does, everywhere we handle route rules within nuxt itself.

prs.title: fix(nitro): respect `sensitive` when matching server route rules
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description with `router.options.sensitive: false`, `/Admin` renders the same page as `/admin`, but none of the server route rules for `/admin` apply to it: ```ts router: { options: { sensitive: false } }, routeRules: { '/admin/**': { redirect: '/login' }, '/Docs': { headers: { 'x-docs': '1' } }, } ``` we'd highly recommend users keep `sensitive` enabled to match h3's defaults, but this adds some normalisation to keep route rules matching case-insensitively in that case.... ideally this would be a `caseSensitive` option in h3's rules matcher that nitro passes through... 👀

prs.title: fix(nuxt): hash keyed function ids + page import names relative to `rootDir`
prs.author: onmax
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

No issue. Regression from #33446, released in v4.3.0 and v3.21.0. Reproduction: [`onmax/repros` at `repro/nuxt-keyed-functions-absolute-path`](https://github.com/onmax/repros/tree/repro/nuxt-keyed-functions-absolute-path/nuxt-keyed-functions-absolute-path)

### 📚 Description

Keyed functions like `useAsyncData` and `useState` get an auto-generated key when you don't pass one.

Since #33446 that key is a hash of the absolute file path, so it changes with the directory you build in. The same commit built in two places gives different chunk hashes and HTML.

This PR hashes the path relative to `rootDir` again, like the old `composable-keys` plugin did:

```diff
 transform(code, id)
   count = 0
+  relativeID = isAbsolute(id) ? relative(rootDir, id) : id
   for each keyed call with no key
-    key = '$' + hash(`${id}-${++count}`)
+    key = '$' + hash(`${relativeID}-${++count}`)
     append key as the last argument
```

Keys for the first keyed call in `app/pages/index.vue`:

| Built in | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `/home/runner/work/project` | `$2h7GcfUpwJ` | `$orW8SXrfeA` |
| `/builds/project` | `$5KDxdpXAPq` | `$orW8SXrfeA` |

This PR should target Nuxt nightly and Nuxt 4

prs.title: fix(nuxt): don't treat constrained route rules as covering dynamic pages
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description a route rule with a regex-constrained param currently counts as covering an entire dynamic page, even though it only matches a subset of the values that page accepts ```ts routeRules: { '/foo/:x([a-z_]+)': { ssr: false }, } ``` with `pages/foo/[x].vue`, `/foo/123` doesn't match that rule at runtime, but the page is still treated as covered, for the purposes of stubbing it out of the `ssr: false` bundle now we treat a regex-constrained param in a route rule as never covering a dynamic page segment, erring on the side of under-coverage

prs.title: fix(nuxt): include `shared/` in build cache hash
prs.author: onmax
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description With `experimental.buildCache`, editing a file in `shared/` could still give a cache hit and restore the old build. `getVueHash` hashes files under each layer's `srcDir`. `shared/` resolves from the layer root, not from `srcDir`. In a project with an `app/` directory, `srcDir` is `app/` and `shared/` sits next to it, so the hash never saw files in `shared/`. This change resolves the layer's shared dir (`dir.shared`, default `shared`) against `rootDir`. If it falls outside `srcDir`, it is hashed as a second `cwd`. To support this, `GetHashOptions['cwd']` now accepts `string | string[]`. I made this repro: https://github.com/onmax/repros/tree/repro/nuxt-build-cache-shared-dir/nuxt-build-cache-shared-dir ```bash git clone --branch repro/nuxt-build-cache-shared-dir https://github.com/onmax/repros.git cd repros node verify.mjs ```

prs.title: fix(nuxt,vite): restore client build state on build cache hits
prs.author: onmax
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

No issue. Reproduction: [`onmax/repros` at `repro/nuxt-build-cache-inlined-css`](https://github.com/onmax/repros/tree/repro/nuxt-build-cache-inlined-css/nuxt-build-cache-inlined-css)

### 📚 Description

With `experimental.buildCache`, a cache hit skips the client build and restores its files from the cache. But the ssr build also reads state that the client build keeps in memory:

- the `ssr-styles` maps (`clientCSSMap`, `clientImporters`, `cssSourcesByCSSFile`)
- the entry file name from `stable-entry`
- the raw client manifest, which `build:manifest` finalises

Only the final `clientManifest`, `clientPrecomputed` and `entryChunkName` strings were replayed. On a cache hit, the ssr build saw empty maps and emitted no render-time `inlinedCSS` conditions, so pages kept `<link rel="stylesheet">` tags for CSS they had already inlined. The HTML differed from a cold build.

The reproduction builds a page with a scoped style twice, once cold and once from the cache. The cold build inlines the style and links no stylesheet. The cache-hit build on main also links `pages.<hash>.css`; with this PR (from pkg.pr.new) it renders the same HTML as the cold build:

```sh
git clone --branch repro/nuxt-build-cache-inlined-css https://github.com/onmax/repros
cd repros && node verify.mjs
```

This PR:

1. adds an internal `addClientBuildState(key, { save, restore })` to `@nuxt/kit/internal`
2. registers the state of `ssr-styles`, `stable-entry` and `client-manifest` with it

prs.title: fix(nuxt): tree-shake auto-imported `#app` composables
prs.author: onmax
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue No issue. Reproduction: [`onmax/repros` at `repro/nuxt-definepagemeta-treeshake`](https://github.com/onmax/repros/tree/repro/nuxt-definepagemeta-treeshake/nuxt-definepagemeta-treeshake) ### 📚 Description `TreeShakeComposablesPlugin` skips `definePageMeta`, `definePayloadReducer`, `definePayloadReviver` and `onPrehydrate` when they're auto-imported. The defaults in `optimization.treeShake.composables` list them under `#app` only, but auto-imports bring them in from subpaths: - `definePageMeta` from `#app/composables/pages` - `definePayloadReducer` and `definePayloadReviver` from `#app/composables/payload` - `onPrehydrate` from `#app/composables/ssr` Since v4.1.1, every page chunk keeps its `definePageMeta()` call and import, on the client and the server. This also affects `4.x`. ```sh git clone --depth 1 --branch repro/nuxt-definepagemeta-treeshake https://github.com/onmax/repros.git cd repros/nuxt-definepagemeta-treeshake pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm verify ``` this PR makes the tree-shake plugin check the auto-import registry, so a composable listed under `#app` is also tree-shaken when it's imported from the subpath it's auto-imported from (like `#app/composables/pages`). it works the same way for any other configured import path, and the defaults stay as they are, so removing a name from `#app` still opts out.

prs.title: perf(vite): pass `serverEntry` to `ServerEntryPlugin`
prs.author: onmax
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue No issue. Reproduction: [`onmax/repros` at `repro/nuxt-spa-full-server-bundle`](https://github.com/onmax/repros/tree/repro/nuxt-spa-full-server-bundle/nuxt-spa-full-server-bundle) ### 📚 Description When the nitro Vite environment is on (the default with the Vite build), `buildsSeparately` is false, and in that mode `ServerEntryPlugin` uses whatever entry it receives as the server entry. Since it receives the full app entry, the whole app goes into the server bundle, even though the server only sends the SPA shell. On a generated 12-layer app with `ssr: false`, the SSR environment goes from 5,332 modules in 12.0 s to 104 modules in 0.3 s, and the whole build from 30.6 s to 15.1 s. The reproduction checks that page and component code stays out of `.output/server`, and that the server still sends the same SPA shell: ```sh git clone --depth 1 --branch repro/nuxt-spa-full-server-bundle https://github.com/onmax/repros.git cd repros/nuxt-spa-full-server-bundle pnpm install && pnpm verify ``` Related #35604

prs.title: fix(nitro): follow module virtuals instead of aliased files in compat scan
prs.author: MaksZhukov
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

Closes #36648

### 📚 Description

When the Nitro compat layer works out which module code the server build reaches, it walks the import graph of the registered entries. A module virtual such as `#meta/nitro` was resolved there like any other specifier, through `resolveAlias`. So when a module also defined a `#meta` alias:

- **Directory alias:** `#meta/nitro` resolved to `<dir>/nitro.ts`. The scan then attributed that file, and its `h3` import, to the server build, which reported a false `NUXT_B9003` and bundled the compat runtime plugins. The build itself loads the virtual, so the file is never bundled.
- **File alias:** resolving `<file>/nitro` threw `ENOTDIR` from `resolveModulePath` in `registrationPaths`.

The fix returns module virtuals by their id in both `registrationPaths` and `resolveScopeImport`. This matches what the build does. `reachableFiles` already reads virtuals from `virtualSources` by id, so their contents are still scanned. The check uses `isModuleVirtual`, so virtuals with deferred (function) templates are covered too.

### How to test

The two regression cases come from @OrbisK's #36619, turned from `it.fails` into normal tests. Both fail without the change and pass with it:

```sh
pnpm vitest run --project unit packages/nitro-server/test/compat.test.ts
```

I ran all `packages/nitro-server` unit tests, ESLint on the changed files, and `vue-tsc --noEmit`. All pass except `nitro-config.test.ts > emits valid single-segment URLPattern

prs.title: perf(nitro): register server auto-imports plugin once
prs.author: onmax
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue No issue. Reproduction: [`onmax/repros` at `repro/nuxt-server-auto-imports-twice`](https://github.com/onmax/repros/tree/repro/nuxt-server-auto-imports-twice/nuxt-server-auto-imports-twice) ### 📚 Description Now nitro passes `rollupConfig.plugins` to the `nitro` Vite environment, so the extra Vite copy made the plugin run twice on every server module. Also skip the `ssr` environment's output in `/vite/services/`, which the app's auto-imports have already transformed. The Rollup copy needs to stay since the prerender build only sees `rollupConfig`; without it you get `ReferenceError: xxxx is not defined`. On a generated 12-layer app, the nitro build step goes from 7.05 s to 3.4 s, and `.output` is identical. The reproduction lists two active copies of `nuxt:server-auto-imports` in the nitro environment, and one with this change. Both builds give the same `.output` (63 of 63 files equal after normalizing): ```sh git clone --depth 1 --branch repro/nuxt-server-auto-imports-twice https://github.com/onmax/repros.git cd repros && node verify.mjs ```

prs.title: perf(vite): avoid quadratic nested dir check for `fs.allow`
prs.author: onmax
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description `allowDirs` gets one entry per component, plugin, middleware and layout directory, so large apps have thousands of entries, mostly repeats. Nested dirs were removed by comparing every entry with every other entry, and duplicates were only removed at the end. ```diff allowDirs = [appDir, workspaceDir, ...modulesDir, ...layerRoots, ...one dir per component / plugin / middleware / layout] .filter(exists) -for each dir d # n entries, duplicates included - for each other entry o # n again → O(n²) - if d starts with o + "/" - drop d -fs.allow = unique(allowDirs) +unique = Set(allowDirs) # duplicates removed first +for each dir d in unique + for each "/" in d # path depth + if unique has d[0 : that "/"] + drop d # Set lookup → O(n × depth) +fs.allow = allowDirs ``` There is now `removeNestedDirs` helper in `packages/vite/src/utils`. The output is the same as before: | input | before | after | |---|---|---| | `/app/components` when `/app` is in the list | dropped | dropped | | `/app-layer/x` when `/app` is in the list | kept | kept | | `/layer/components` when `/layer/` is in the list | kept | kept | | `/a` listed twice | merged at the end | merged first | In a lab project, the time from `build:before` to `vite:extend` (where `fs.allow` is built), 5,000 components, the time went from 454 ms to 24 ms

prs.title: fix(nuxt): hide RouteLocationRaw from navigateTo's public return type
prs.author: Ibochkarev
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

resolves #36658

### 📚 Description

- The public `navigateTo` type no longer includes `RouteLocationRaw`. Externally, it remains `Promise<void | NavigationFailure | false> | false | void`.
- Internally, the second signature still allows `RouteLocationRaw` because the function still returns the original route from the route middleware, and the redirect runner reads it.
- With experimental.typedPages, the RouteLocationRaw type expands to the union of all routes. A function that returns `navigateTo()` alongside another value runs into TS2590.
- The signature in `docs/4.api/3.utils/navigate-to.md` has been converted to a public type, and it also states that the middleware still returns the route at runtime.

prs.title: fix(vite): skip quoted `import.meta` keys + limit replace to client dev
prs.author: FelixFangX
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue Fixes #36657 ### ❓ Type of change - [x] bugfix ### 📚 Description Vite serves `@vite-ignore` workers as `?worker_file&type=ignore` and injects an env preamble whose `defines` object uses string keys like `"import.meta.envName"`. `nuxt:replace` text-replaced those keys into invalid JS (`""development""`), causing a PARSE_ERROR in dev. Exclude ignore-worker module ids from the replace transform so Vite can handle those modules itself. Normal modules still get `import.meta.*` defines replaced. ### 📝 Checklist - [x] I have linked an issue or discussion. - [x] I have added tests where possible.

prs.title: fix(nuxt): remove purged entries from `_asyncData`
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue resolves #36676 ### 📚 Description once the last component using a key unmounts, its `useAsyncData` entry gets purged but stays in `nuxtApp._asyncData`. it's never reused, but `execute` closes over the options/handler of the last caller, meaning the previous page's setup scope (and anything else there) stays alive... this seems to have been the case since v3.17.

prs.title: perf(nitro,nuxt,rspack,vite-server,webpack): bundle esm vue + reuse caches
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description this is one of several PRs from looking at SSR performance based on a Nuxt UI 4 marketing page, as a stand-in for a reasonably heavy component-focused site ... | | `main` | this PR | delta | | - | - | - | - | | Nuxt UI page (median, µs) | 15551 / 14731 | 11868 / 11761 | -24% / -20% | | static single-SFC page (median, µs) | 412 / 395 | 363 / 358 | -12% / -9% | | static page with webpack (median, µs) | 362 / 355 | 317 / 316 | -12% / -11% | this _significantly_ improves performance by forcing the esm bundler vue build, which has performance optimisations (ie vue feature flags) and also avoids the cjs interop helpers. additionally, this prevents multiple copies of vue being installed, we enable dead-code elimination in nitro with process.env.NODE_ENV` - with nice improvements! | server JS (static page) | `main` | this PR | | - | - | - | | Vite | 837 KB | 700 KB | | Vite (`nitroViteEnvironment: false`) | 914 KB | 732 KB | | webpack | 2.87 MB | 1.54 MB | | rspack | 2.94 MB | 1.72 MB | | `@nuxt/vite-server` | 1.64 MB | 652 KB | and we fix a bug whereby webpack ssr inlining wouldn't have worked at all with optionsApi off... and, finally, we share Vue's `propsCache` and `emitsCache` across requests so we don't have to re-normalise every component's props and emits on a per-request basis... (an extra 3% faster render on the full example ui page - on top of everything else)

prs.title: fix(nuxt): only return redirects from `navigateTo` while middleware runs
prs.author: volkanakyel
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

### 📚 Description

Ran into this when `navigateTo()` from a component just... didn't navigate.

`_processingMiddleware` gets set when a navigation starts, but it's only cleared in `afterEach` / `onError`. So if a navigation is still pending after middleware already ran (a slow `beforeResolve` guard, an async page chunk loading), any `navigateTo()` called from a component during that window returns a route object instead of navigating. The navigation is silently lost.

**Fix:** on the client, clear the flag as soon as Nuxt's middleware guard is done, by registering a `beforeEach` right after it. Applied to both the vue-router plugin and the universal router.

**Heads up on one behavior change:** `navigateTo()` inside a custom `router.beforeResolve` or `onBeforeRouteUpdate` now starts a new navigation instead of returning a redirect location. You end up on the same route either way.

**Tests:** added one per router that reproduces the bug. They fail before this change and pass after.

prs.title: perf(vite): skip compiling plain style blocks in the server build
prs.author: onmax
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

No issue.

### 📚 Description

The server build compiles every `<style>` block of every component and then throws the CSS away. A plain style block (not a CSS module, not `?inline`) reaches the server bundle only as a side-effect import. Its CSS goes through `vite:vue`, `vite:css` and `vite:css-post`, which keeps an empty `no-treeshake` module. With Nitro's Vite builder, `fullstack:assets` also sets `build.emitAssets` on `ssr`, so that CSS is written as `.css` files under `.nuxt/vite/services/ssr`, and nothing copies them to `.output`.

With `features.inlineStyles`, each block is compiled a second time from its `?inline&used` id, which is the copy the renderer inlines. So the first compile is wasted with either setting.

This PR resolves those imports in the `ssr` environment to one empty, side-effect-free module. Styles with exports still compile: CSS modules (the render function reads their class names) and anything with `?inline` (inlined styles, custom elements). `ssr-styles` resolves its `?inline&used` copies with `this.resolve`, which skips the plugin's own hook, so inlining doesn't change.

On a generated app with 12 layers and 2,860 components (1,396 with a scoped style), Nuxt 5 nightly with Vite 8.3.5 and Rolldown 1.2.15:

| | inline styles on, before → after | inline styles off, before → after |
|---|---|---|
| ssr modules | 6,727 → 5,332 | 5,331 → 3,936 |
| ssr output files | 4,886 → 4,126 | 1,937 → 1,177 |
| `vite:vue` transforms in ssr | 5,98
